headline: Brest's 5-1 home win meets Nice's away defeats
summary: Brest host Nice on Friday in Ligue 1, 9 points against 8 in mid-table. Brest's 5-1 home win over Angers is why the market makes them 42.2% favourites across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, while Nice are 29.0% to win and have lost their last two away games. But Brest allowed 2.17 expected goals at Lille on Saturday and are without Raphaël Le Guen, 450 minutes this season, in a back line that is already short. The handicap line is a quarter of a goal, and the goal total has slipped to 2.75 from 2.84.
read: Brest are narrow home favourites at 42.2% against a Nice side that sits one point and three places below them, with the market rating the hosts roughly a quarter of a goal better. Brest's 5-1 home win over Angers is the form behind the price, while Nice arrive off a 2-1 defeat at Lyon in which a stoppage-time equaliser was ruled out by centimetres.

facts.fact: Brest are the favourites at 42.2% to win, with the draw at 28.8% and Nice at 29.0%.
Brest beat Angers 5-1 at home in their last home league game on 10 October.
facts.meaning: It is their only win in their last four league matches — and the reason they are fancied at home.

facts.fact: Brest conceded 2.17 xG at Lille on Saturday, the most they have allowed in their last five matches.
facts.meaning: Their 1-1 draw at Lille came with a warning: they were carved open and Nice's attack will have noticed.

facts.fact: Nice lost 2-1 at Lyon on Sunday and have lost their last two away league matches.
facts.meaning: Away from home Nice have been the weaker side, which is exactly where the market's read of this game points.

facts.fact: Brest are 10th on 9 points, Nice 13th on 8 — one point between them after seven games.
facts.meaning: A mid-table meeting with immediate consequence: the winner moves clear of the other before the weekend's other results.

facts.fact: Brest are without Raphaël Le Guen, who has played 450 minutes this season, because of a broken leg.
facts.meaning: A regular defender is missing, and Brendan Chardonnet is also out with a calf injury, thinning the back line.

facts.fact: Nice's most-used absentee, defender A. Mendy, has played only 124 minutes this season.
facts.meaning: Nice's injury list looks long but is thin on first-team minutes — Olivier Pantaloni has close to a full-strength squad.

facts.fact: The market's goal total has come down from 2.84 to 2.75, with Over 2.75 now at 50.0%.
facts.meaning: About two or three goals is the expectation, and it has edged slightly lower in recent days.

sources.fact: Julien Lachuer said only Brendan Chardonnet and Raphaël Le Guen should miss the visit of Nice through injury.
Giovani Versini stopped training on Wednesday and is doubtful for Nice, though his coach Julien Lachuer has not fully ruled him out of the squad.
Versini returned to training and Baldé is said to be reassuring ahead of the Nice match.
Olivier Pantaloni wants to neutralise Brest striker Ludovic Ajorque, whose statistics are highlighted as a threat.
Brest drew 1-1 at Lille on Saturday, again pairing Gautier Lloris and Lucas Tousart in central defence.
Brest were sanctioned by the LFP disciplinary commission on Wednesday 21 October, with the details of the sanction listed by the outlet.
Nice lost 2-1 at Lyon on Sunday in Ligue 1's 7th round and remain 13th in the table.
Nice had a goal by Wahi ruled out for a matter of centimetres in stoppage time at Lyon.
